tests.reason: The PostgREST-Aurora proxy's nginx routing has no staging endpoint yet (the prod proxy and its public host come from the dispatch-only workflows of VTID-05023). This builds the real image and proves both audiences against a mock Supabase: internal passthrough of auth/storage/functions/realtime (websocket upgrade, 30 MB upload, 50 MB functions cap), /rest to PostgREST, 501 for unknown paths; on the public host only /rest and /alive, and no request reaches Supabase. It fails on the previous config.

Part 0 privilege-parity gate: diff and fix generation over fixture catalogs (anon EXECUTE on increment_wallet_balance flagged and revoked, RLS off fixed, statement_timeout mismatch, quoting). The gate itself runs against the Aurora clone and Aurora, never as a staging test.

auth-bridge webhook is mounted and refuses a call without the service token (rejected write probe)

tests.reason: R1(b) gateway part: SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL. With SUPABASE_URL on the internal proxy origin and SUPABASE_PUBLIC_URL on supabase.co, storage public URLs, signed URLs, the video thumbnail URL and GET /auth/config come out on the public origin and never contain the internal host; a guard fails on any new getPublicUrl/createSignedUrl call site not routed through the helper. Staging still runs with SUPABASE_URL on supabase.co, so the HTTP probe above proves today's value is unchanged.

Part 6 side effects (side-effects.md A + B). Nothing here runs on staging or touches a live database: on a throwaway local Postgres it applies scripts/aws/aurora-cutover-outbox.sql and aurora-cutover-cron.sql line by line, twice, and proves the Aurora trigger functions queue the Supabase URL/headers/body with secret references only, RLS keeps anon/authenticated out, the claim/complete/fail RPCs (SKIP LOCKED, lease, backoff, 5 attempts), the 21 cron jobs with byte-exact commands and schedules, the Supabase unschedule + rollback (all 25 jobs back identical, triggers re-enabled), the cluster-params script against a fake aws (dry run changes nothing, --apply never reboots), and that the scheduled-edge-calls workflow parses. WITH_PG_CRON=1 adds real pg_cron in docker.

Part 6 outbox sender (services/gateway/src/services/outbound-http-worker.ts): claim, send, retry with backoff, final after 5 attempts, idempotency per row id, header-reference resolution from an allowlist, allowed destinations only, no secret in logs or last_error. The worker ships off (OUTBOUND_HTTP_WORKER_ENABLED unset, never on staging), so there is nothing to probe on staging; the /alive probe above proves the gateway still boots with the new wiring.

Part 4 auth->Aurora bridge, gateway side. POST /api/v1/internal/auth-bridge/user-event has no member-visible staging behaviour and must not be exercised on staging (staging shares production's Supabase; every call writes). The suite proves the service-token gate (401 without/with a wrong token and whenever GATEWAY_SERVICE_TOKEN is unset), INSERT and confirm-UPDATE provisioning with active_tenant_id written back only when missing, other UPDATEs ignored, DELETE cleanup, idempotency and loud 500s; the reconciler (provisions missing users created since AUTH_BRIDGE_RECONCILE_SINCE, pages GoTrue to the end, cleans users deleted on Supabase only after a GoTrue 404, aborts on a failed page, caps deletions, off by default and never on staging); ensureProvisioned() (inert unless AUTH_BRIDGE_ENABLED=true, cached, never throws); and that the eight post-sign-up write paths await it before their first member write.

Part 4 auth->Aurora bridge, Aurora side, on throwaway local Postgres (no staging database runs the bridge before the window): the real scripts/aws/aurora-cutover-auth-bridge.sql applied twice over Aurora's auth shim; ensure_provisioned() creates exactly the rows Supabase's six auth.users triggers create (verbatim copies, diffed row by row) and a second call creates nothing; the PostgREST db-pre-request hook is a no-op in a read-only (GET) transaction and for a null uid or service_role, an unprovisioned member's GET succeeds, their first write succeeds after the hook provisions (and fails on the app_users FK without it), service accounts are skipped, a provisioning failure never fails the request; deletion applies CASCADE / SET NULL / the contacts cleanup, reports NO ACTION rows, refuses an empty FK map and is idempotent; members cannot execute the service-role functions.

Part 7a: the self-hosted Realtime server has no staging endpoint (it is deployed only by the dispatch-only AWS-PROD-DEPLOY-REALTIME-AURORA.yml after the Aurora reboot). This builds the real image (pinned supabase/realtime v2.134.10 + Vitana seeds.exs) and runs it against a local Postgres 17 with logical decoding, wal2json and TLS-only logins, after applying scripts/aws/aurora-realtime-setup.sql unchanged as a non-superuser role: management API refuses member tokens (separate secret), websocket upgrade 101/401/404 by token and Host, and a @supabase/realtime-js client on Host realtime.vitanaland.com receives an RLS-filtered INSERT, an UPDATE with the old row, broadcast and presence, again after a restart. It also applies the 33-table publication part twice and checks the primary-key precondition.

Parts 8b + 12(i): the Aurora->Supabase CDC tasks have no staging counterpart (they run only in the window, against production Supabase) and must not be exercised on staging. On a throwaway local Postgres this proves supabase-cutover-reverse-cdc-triggers.sql disables every public user trigger (FK and non-public triggers untouched, snapshot not overwritten on re-run), that a row applied the way DMS applies it fires no notification and keeps its updated_at, and that the rollback restores every trigger's exact prior state (O, D, A) and refuses without a snapshot; with a fake aws it proves aurora-to-supabase-cdc.sh builds the 5-table storage-auth and the all-other-tables rollback mappings, creates a CDC-only task without starting it, sets no replica mode, and never puts a password on a command line or leaves it on disk.

Part 8 migration workflows to Aurora. Nothing here runs on staging or touches a live database: migrations reach Aurora only through RUN-MIGRATION.yml with MIGRATION_TARGET=aurora, a window step. On a throwaway local Postgres with a fake aws CLI it proves scripts/aws/aurora-apply-migration.sh: a good file commits all statements in one Data API transaction (the file's BEGIN/COMMIT dropped) and sends NOTIFY pgrst afterwards; a failing 3rd statement or a failure at COMMIT leaves the database unchanged and exits non-zero naming the statement; non-transactional statements are refused without --allow-non-transactional; dry run, psql meta-commands, a top-level ROLLBACK, a wrong account and MIGRATION_FREEZE=true make no rds-data call. The pgrst DDL watch, applied twice line by line, notifies on CREATE/ALTER/DROP. Both workflows parse and resolve input > MIGRATION_TARGET > supabase and fail fast under MIGRATION_FREEZE. The splitter is unit-tested on comments, quoting and dollar quotes, swept over every supabase/migrations file, and matches psql (statement count and pg_dump --schema-only) on 15 real migrations.

Part 10 prep: the Aurora clone workflow is dispatch-only and creates nothing on merge. With a fake aws (no network) this proves create never modifies vitana-aurora-prod (production appears only as the restore and parameter-group source), the clone gets its own parameter group copy, delete refuses vitana-aurora-prod and every other name before any AWS call and refuses an untagged cluster, dry runs change nothing, and the workflow makes no AWS call of its own besides the account check; mutation-checked five ways.
